newsitem.title: USA: Sri Lanka poised to regain tea market - World Bank.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka poised to regain tea market - World Bank.

text.p: Sri Lanka's tea industry is primed to regain its former dominance in the global black tea market, the World Bank said Monday.

The bank, in a report entitled "Sri Lanka's Tea Industry: Succeeding in the Global Market," said Sri Lanka's tea production was benefiting from the deregulation and privatization of its publicly owned plantation companies.
The report called on the government and the recently privatized tea companies to move away from mass marketing of its teas and to instead focus on its core markets.

"Sri Lanka holds a strong position as a leading exporter of black tea, has a diversified product line, good quality control within the industry, and an image that is strong in the international tea market," Ridwan Ali, the World Bank's South Asia rural development manager, said in a statement.
Sri Lanka produced 258.4 million kg of tea last year, but officials said last month plantations would produce at least 50 percent more tea annually per hectare in 10 years time.
Tea was once a major agricultural commodity in Sri Lanka that spurred its economic growth, and was a main source of its foreign exchange earnings, the bank said.

However, a 67 percent drop in the world prices for tea from 1970 to 1995, and tight state control of the industry, took a heavy toll on its export earnings and the tea industry as a whole, the bank said.
